_why: Known coverage gaps, accepted for now, each with a reason. Same ratchet shape as
tools/prose-baseline.txt and tools/trace-baseline.txt: a gap listed here does not
fail the build, a gap NOT listed here does, and a gap that grows fails even if it
is listed (the check compares `missing` against the recorded number).
These are content gaps, not defects in the shipped experience: a domain with no
Build Lab still teaches and still gates. They are recorded so they cannot be
mistaken for covered ground, which is exactly what happened to cloud-platform's
check bank — 0 of 290 checks, invisible to every validator, for a whole release.
Do NOT add a line here to make a build pass. Author the content, or record why
the gap is the right call.

build:technical-depth.note: The 6 authored builds are architecture-assembly challenges, which suit systems/AI material. Big-O, storage engines and concurrency are better served by the interactive widgets this domain already has 21 of. A build here needs a different lab TYPE (tradeoff configuration or failure diagnosis, section 6.4), not another topology to assemble.

build:direction-influence.note: The Architecture Builder grades a component graph, and this domain teaches influence and technical strategy — there is no topology to assemble. The right lab type is Architecture Review or a written-rationale defence (section 34.2), neither of which exists yet.

build:leveling-scope.note: Same reason as direction-influence: scope and leverage are not a graph. Open, and it is the clearest argument for adding the Migration Design lab type.

build:cloud-platform.note: This one SHOULD have builds and does not — landing zones, cell-based architecture and private network paths are exactly what the existing Architecture Builder grades well. It is the highest-value entry in this file. Not authored in this pass because the 26-concept check bank came first.

codex:direction-influence.note: The Codex is deliberately scoped to AI-architecture vocabulary (see CLAUDE.md), so it holds no entries about influence or technical strategy. A cross-link floor is the wrong rule for this domain rather than a gap in it — but it is recorded rather than special-cased in the checker, because if the Codex ever broadens, this should start failing.

codex:leveling-scope.note: Same as direction-influence: the reference layer does not cover seniority and scope, by design.
